title: Ham Crawford's travels, and first hearing of Wingy and the Crescent City Jazzers
summary: Crawford recruited the best young local players; Kelly first heard of Wingy from a New Orleans band photo and recalls the Riddick brothers.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: I think I didn't ask you something I wanted to about Ham Crawford. I believe it was Wingy, and I, this has been several months back, uh, since I even read the book. But he mentioned Wenslow, Arizona, Ham being out there.

Um, Ham played all out through the West. And when he was with him for a time, when he was also out there with Doc Ross for a time, we talked about that. But, uh, Ham Crawford, uh, organized little bands and took them everywhere. And somehow he would just end up, he'd come into a town and pick all the best musicians and offer them wonderful, a wonderful future. And sometimes it materialized, sometimes it didn't. But at least he always was able to attract the best of the young musicians, because they're always ready to leave home, you know. Just a chance to play, that's the thing. Oh, sure.
And, uh, did he, did you and Wingy work with him at the same time? No.

No. I didn't meet Wingy until several years later. Uh-huh. And, uh, I met him in Shreveport. And I had first heard of Wingy when I was playing with the Budysburg Mountain Boys. And I remember a little drug store over in Meridian where we looked at a picture of a wild New Orleans band, all posed and everything. And of course we were attracted to it and so we asked who they were and we called them the Crescent City Jazzers or something like that, from Mobile.

And, uh, Wingy was the trumpet player. I remember the other people, but that's my first, uh, knowledge of Wingy. And then, of course, historically I've known Wingy closely and well over a period of, uh, more than 50 years.
I think almost all those Crescent City Jazzers ago. Jeff Riddick's brother, Johnny, played with him at one time.
That's right. And I knew Johnny. He was a band harmonica player, if I'm not mistaken, also. Really?

And, uh, and one of the Riddicks, of course I knew Jeff through his affiliation with Wildlands and the Warriors, and I knew him more so as a player. Yeah. He's, he's a good, well-routined New Orleans piano player.
